family.description: This domain is found in diverse bacterial signaling proteins. It is called EAL after its conserved residues. The EAL domain is a good candidate for a diguanylate phosphodiesterase function [[cite:PUB00007150]]. The domain contains many conserved acidic residues that could participate in metal binding and might form the phosphodiesterase active site [[cite:PUB00007150]].
family.name: EAL domain
